claims.claim: Tomcat's default pool is 200 threads, which matches the ~200 waiting requests per pod in the load test
claims.why: The benchmark doesn't measure thread-pool size or the most requests that can wait at once: its I/O-wait test used only 256 connections with a 10 ms wait, and java-spring still served 15,611 req/s.

claims.claim: Tomcat's default max-connections is 8192, raised to 12000 so it can hold the waiting partners' open connections
claims.why: No test went above 256 connections, so the benchmark says nothing about connection limits in the thousands.

claims.claim: Holding 10,000 open connections needs enough file descriptors and pod memory
claims.measured: java-spring peak memory 491 MB at 256 connections in the I/O-wait test
claims.why: The claim gives no figure, and the measurements only go up to 256 connections, so the memory needed for 10,000 can't be checked.
